#en: I remember when cutters like the Prairiefire still came through Gagarin shining. Fresh paint, clean manifests, Trackers stepping off the ramp like they were the sharp end of justice. We used to turn those ships around in under six hours; grab a TerraBrew, grease a few couplings, stamp the contracts and wave them back to the stars. Somewhere between then and now, the jobs got stranger. Line items turned vague. Storm delays that should have cost weeks just stopped happening, and nobody upstairs wanted to hear why. "Temporary measures," they said. "Just until the grids stabilize."  \n\nLast month I pulled an overnight in the annex and found a string of old climate files misfiled under security footage, all tagged with the same consulting alias. Freight that always left on the wrong side of a cyclone and arrived bone-dry. At first I thought it was just us screwing up, some lazy clerk hiding mistakes where no one would look. But the more I dug, the more it felt like something that had been small once, half a workaround, half a favor, and then never stopped growing. Now the Prairiefire is parked out there like a bad memory, and her logs are the only place left where you can see how a lot of people quietly decided not to fix what they never meant to start.
zh: 我记得草原火号那类切割船还会光鲜地开进加加林的日子。新漆、干净的清单，追踪者联盟的人走下舷梯，像他们是正义的锋刃。我们那时能在六小时内让那些船掉头；拿杯地球酿酒，给几个接头加点油，盖上章，挥手把他们送回星海。不知从那时到现在之间的某个时候，活儿变了味。条目变得含糊。本该耗费数周的风暴延误干脆不再发生，而楼上没人想听原因。"临时措施，"他们说，"等电网稳定下来就撤。"\n\n上个月我在附楼熬了个通宵，发现一串旧气候文件被错归在安保录像底下，全都带着同一个顾问化名。那些货物总是在气旋的错误一侧离开，却干爽无恙地抵达。起初我以为只是我们在搞砸，某个懒文员把错误藏到没人会看的地方。可我挖得越深，就越觉得这东西曾经很小——一半是权宜之计，一半是人情——然后一直不停地生长。如今草原火号就那么停在外面，像一段糟糕的记忆，而她的日志是仅存的地方，让你看清许多人如何悄悄决定不去修那些他们从未打算开始的事。

#en: I am recording this from a maintenance crawlspace two decks above the cargo ring, knees jammed against conduit, watching the relay's traffic map bleed red where it should be clean. Took me three days of sipping recycled air and pretending to be another overworked tech before the broker stopped flinching every time I walked past their office. They talked plenty about shell firms and "risk partners," but whenever certain names came up, they did not say them; they just tapped a knuckle on the table, or glanced at the ceiling, or said, "You know who" and moved on. That is how you know you are close to the real monsters, when people start speaking in silhouettes instead of words.\n\nThe manifests themselves were the key. Buried behind the usual Trade Authority double-talk, I found a sequence of scrap lots and "noncompliant hulls" diverted to a single disposal ring out past any profitable orbit. I cross-checked the beacon fingerprints we pulled from that Dogstar mess with the relay's routing history, and there it was the same corrupted signature, over and over, terminating at one dead Deimos facility nobody has paid to decommission. The broker pretended not to see it when I laid the pattern out. They just went quiet, closed the ledger, and asked if we were done.
zh: 我在货舱环上方两层的一条维护爬行通道里录下这些，膝盖顶着导管，看着中继站的交通图上本该干净的地方渗出红色。我花了三天啜着再循环空气、假装自己是又一个累坏的技工，那经纪商才不再每次我走过他们办公室时就一哆嗦。他们对空壳公司和"风险伙伴"侃侃而谈，可每当某些名字被提起，他们就不说出来；他们只是用指节敲敲桌子，或瞟一眼天花板，或者说一句"你知道是谁"然后就翻篇。这就是你接近真正的怪物时的迹象——人们开始用剪影说话，而不是用词。\n\n清单本身就是关键。埋在贸易管理局惯常的双关话术后面，我发现一连串废料批次和"不合规船体"被转运到任何有利可图的轨道之外一个单一的处置环。我把我们从那个狗星乱局里取到的信标指纹与中继站的路由历史交叉核对，它就在那儿——同一个损坏的特征，一遍又一遍，终结在一座没人出钱退役的废弃火卫二设施。当我把图案铺开时，那经纪商假装没看见。他们只是沉默下来，合上账簿，问我们是不是问完了。

#en:
I am writing this down so I remember I was not imagining it.

Neon's docks always feel like waking up mid-fall: noise, light, fuel stink, everyone pretending the chaos is planned. Tonight felt different. A berth that had been "blocked for maintenance" all week suddenly went green the second a hauler without a visible queue code drifted in. No hails, no argument over fees, just a tired clerk thumbing an override like muscle memory while the loadmaster stared a little too hard at the floor.

When I asked about it later, I got three answers from three people. Emergency medical relief. VIP corporate shipment. System glitch. Same ship, same berth, three stories that did not quite fit together. It reminded me of the time back in 2328 when we rushed a clearance on a freighter because some supervisor did not want to stay late. Only later did anyone notice that half its cargo never existed in the registry.

I am starting with almost nothing a dead slate I pulled off a derelict and a name that keeps changing in people's mouths whenever they talk about vanished debts and ships that always seem to leave on time. Whatever happened in haste back then is still echoing through these berths, and whoever is pulling the strings is counting on the rest of us being too tired to notice.
zh:
我把这个写下来，好让自己记得我并非在凭空想象。

霓虹城的码头总像在半坠中醒来：噪声、灯光、燃料的臭气，人人假装这混乱是计划好的。今晚感觉不同。一个整周都"因维护封闭"的泊位，在一艘看不到排队代码的货船刚一漂进来时忽然转绿。没有呼叫，没有为费用争执，只有一个疲惫的文员像凭肌肉记忆一样按下越权键，而装货长盯着地板盯得有点太用力。

后来我问起这事，从三个人那儿得到三个答案。紧急医疗救济。企业贵宾货运。系统故障。同一艘船，同一个泊位，三个拼不太到一起的说法。它让我想起 2328 年那次，我们因为某个主管不想加班而给一艘货船加急放行。事后才有人注意到，它一半的货物在登记册里根本不存在。

我手头几乎什么都没有——一块我从弃船上取下的死数据板，和一个每当人们谈起消失的债务、以及那些似乎总能准时离开的飞船时就在他们嘴里变来变去的名字。当年匆忙之间发生的事仍在这些泊位间回响，而那个牵线的人，正指望我们其余人累得察觉不到。

#en:
I am recording this because nobody down here says anything straight, and I need at least one thing that is not twisted by three different mouths before breakfast.

I am sitting on a crate in the salvage pit, boots in coolant, holding a half-melted datapack I did not pay enough for. Rafe swears he pulled it off a hauler that "just spun apart" near an old war corridor. He says he heard the job from a spacer who heard it from a GalBank courier who heard it from some UC tech. Every time I ask for a name, the story jumps one link further away, like everyone is afraid to admit they were this close to it.

The casing is cooked, but the nav buffer inside is not dead yet. I scraped enough out to see a route stub, pointed right at a vault ship that has been dark longer than GalBank likes to admit. Same harmonics tag I caught on those redacted test logs years ago, same pattern in the drive entries that nobody wanted to hear about. I followed a ghost signature from a forgotten outpost to a dead freight yard and then into Neon's pipes; now the broken trail in this pack lines up with that vault's last declared jump. Whatever she is tracking, whatever she is trying to prove, the next piece of it is locked in that floating bank the galaxies pretend is still just "under maintenance."
zh:
我录下这个，因为这下面没人把话说直，而我在吃早饭之前至少需要一件没被三张不同的嘴拧过的事。

我坐在打捞坑里的一只板条箱上，靴子泡在冷却液里，手里攥着一个我没花够钱买的半熔数据包。拉夫赌咒说他是从一艘在旧战争走廊附近"就那么转散了"的货船上取下来的。他说这活儿他是从一个太空人那儿听来的，太空人又是从一个银河银行快船员那儿听来的，快船员又是从某个联殖技工那儿听来的。每次我追问一个名字，故事就再往远处跳一节，像人人都害怕承认自己曾离它这么近。

外壳烧焦了，可里面的导航缓冲还没死。我刮出了足够多，看见一段航路存根，直指一艘沉寂得比银河银行愿意承认的更久的金库船。和我多年前在那些涂黑测试日志上抓到的同一标签，和那些没人愿意听的驱动条目里同样的图案。我从一座被遗忘的前哨站顺着一个幽灵特征追到一个死货运场，再追进霓虹城的管道；如今这个数据包里断裂的痕迹，与那艘金库船最后一次申报的跃迁吻合。不管她在追踪什么、想证明什么，它的下一块碎片锁在那座漂在太空、被各星系假装只是"维护中"的银行里。

#en:
I am recording this mostly so I can convince myself I did not imagine it.

Soil is not supposed to pull like that. You stand still and you can feel your weight slide a fraction sideways, like the ground is remembering a different center. The miners who were here before me turned it into a bar story, something to tell over cheap liquor about "crooked gravity" and tools that fell in the wrong direction. Funny how none of them ever wrote it down. The old survey logs skirt around it with phrases like "localized anomaly," then change the subject. Same with the rig failures, and the missing warning pings from that relay everyone pretends never existed.

The thing we dug up today hums with the same wrongness. Not loud, just enough that if you hold it long enough your fingers go numb. The foreman made a point of saying we were not to speculate about it over open comms, and the rest of the crew nodded like they had already made that agreement without me. Nobody mentioned the failed crops on that moon, or the storm beacons that drifted off target, or the quiet talk that some engineer somewhere is learning how to teach gravity new tricks. Those parts stay unspoken, but they are there, hanging in the air with the rust and the coolant, waiting for someone stubborn enough to pull on them.
zh:
我录下这个，主要是为了说服自己我并非凭空想象。

土壤不该那么拉扯。你站着不动，就能感觉到自己的重量朝侧面滑了一丝，像地面记着另一个中心。在我之前待在这儿的矿工把它变成了酒吧故事，就着廉价烈酒讲的那种——关于"歪斜的重力"和朝错误方向掉落的工具。有趣的是，他们谁也没把它写下来。旧勘测日志用"局部异常"这种说法绕着它走，然后换话题。装备故障、以及那座人人都假装从未存在的中继站丢失的警告探测，也是一样。

我们今天挖出来的东西，也带着同样的一种"不对"。声音不大，可你攥得够久，手指就会发麻。工头特意强调不许在公开通讯上议论它，其余船员都点头，像他们已经背着我达成了那个约定。没人提起那颗卫星上歉收的庄稼，没人提起漂离目标的暴风信标，也没人提起那种悄悄话——说某个工程师正在学着教重力玩新把戏。这些部分没人说出口，可它们就在那儿，和锈迹、冷却液一起悬在空气里，等着哪个够固执的人去扯一扯。

#en:
They told me this posting was temporary. Six months underground, eyes on a dead corridor of space, then back to daylight work. That was three years and a dozen "routine extensions" ago. Somewhere along the way, the filters we flagged as provisional stayed, the back channels stayed, I stayed. Temporary turned into default, and nobody sent an update.

Today I finally saw why.

I was combing archived feeds, trying to prove to myself that all this quiet meant something, when I found the pattern. Same consultant ID buried in environmental telemetry from frontier farms, from a clinic that should not have had that kind of tuning, from an old weapons bay listed as decommissioned. Cross checked it against a blacked out operations file I was never supposed to open. There she was, walking through a restricted asset like she had clearance, under cover of one of our own codenames.

Followed the signal out, past the redactions. It terminates in a cargo registry marked as scrap, a hangar written off on every official chart I can access. Nothing is ever really gone; they just stop printing it. That hangar is where her trail surfaces again. I have tagged the coordinates and locked them in this log. If someone is finally hunting her, they will need a starting point that is not already a lie.
zh:
他们告诉我这个岗位是临时的。地下六个月，盯着一截死掉的太空走廊，然后回去干见天日的活儿。那是三年和十几次"例行延期"之前了。一路上不知何时，我们标记为临时的过滤器留了下来，后门频道留了下来，我也留了下来。临时变成了默认，而没人发来一份更新。

今天我总算看清了为什么。

我翻检存档数据流，想向自己证明这一切安静意味着什么，这时我发现了那个图案。同一个顾问 ID，埋在外缘农场的环境遥测里，埋在一家本不该有那种调校的诊所里，埋在一个被列为已退役的旧武器舱里。我把它和一份我本不该打开的涂黑作战文件交叉核对。她就在那里，像有通行权限一样走过一处受限资产，用我们自己的一个代号作掩护。

我顺着信号追出去，穿过那些涂黑。它终结在一份被标为废料的货运登记册里，一座在我能查到的每一张官方星图上都被注销的机库。没有东西真的消失；他们只是不再印它。那座机库就是她的痕迹再次浮现的地方。我把坐标标注出来，锁进这份日志。要是终于有人在追捕她，他们会需要一个不已经是谎言的起点。

#en:
They told us the war was over before I was old enough to hold a rifle, but the dust out by the old trench line never got that message. I was hauling scrap plating for Salvage Crown Union when my cutter snagged something half-buried, a dataslate wedged under a rusted bunk frame. Should have logged it as waste, tossed it in with the rest, but the power light was still blinking and curiosity buys more trouble than credits out here.

The rosters inside do not match what they taught us in school. Names marked evacuated the day my father never came home. Medical sign-offs all bearing the same neat hand, attached to casualty clusters that locals swear were left screaming in the dirt. It looks like someone meant to come back, clean up the numbers, finish erasing whatever really happened in those barracks. The last entries are flagged for review, then nothing. No follow-up, no closure, just a frozen list of ghosts and a medic's signature that keeps turning up in backroom stories from Akila to New Atlantis.

I have been chewing on this all shift. Part of me wants to dump the slate in a GalBank drop and pretend I never saw it. The other part keeps thinking if those numbers can be bent once, they can be bent again. To hide the dead. Or to hide someone who is not as dead as they are supposed to be.
zh:
他们告诉我们战争结束了，那时我还小到拿不动一支步枪，可旧战壕线那儿的尘土从没收到这条消息。我当时在为打捞王冠工会拖运废铁板，我的切割船勾到了半埋在锈蚀床架底下的东西——一块卡在那儿的数据板。本该把它记成废料，和其他东西一起扔掉的，可它的电源灯还在闪，而在这外面好奇心招来的麻烦比信用币多。

里面的人员名册和学校里教我们的对不上。有些名字被标记为"已撤离"，而那天正是我父亲再没回家的日子。医疗签核全出自同一只工整的手，附在那些据本地人赌咒说曾被丢在尘土里惨叫的伤亡群体上。看起来像有人打算回来，把数字清理干净，把那些兵营里真正发生过的事彻底抹掉。最后几条被标记为待复核，然后什么都没有了。没有跟进，没有结案，只有一张冻住的鬼名单，和一个不断从阿基拉传到新亚特兰蒂斯的密室故事里冒出来的军医签名。

我整个班都在琢磨这事。我有一部分想把数据板丢进银河银行的投递箱，假装从没见过。另一部分不停在想：如果那些数字能被弯一次，就能被再弯一次。用来藏死者。或者藏一个没他该有的那么死的人。

#en: Among independent haulers operating in the same lanes as the derelict Tidewalker TA-7207, few names come up as often as Second Flight. The crew is known for taking contracts other captains quietly decline, running cargo and salvage through routes where patrol coverage thins out and navigation data stops lining up cleanly with official charts. They are not registered as a guild, nor do they maintain a fixed home port, but their transponder sig has been logged in proximity to more than one "administratively unresolved" incident near Trade Authority assets.\n\nThe name Second Flight is widely believed to reference a failed first venture, though records of any earlier ship under their banner are conspicuously absent from standard registries. What is documented is a pattern: whenever a cargo hull goes dark in that sector, Second Flight is never far from the next set of sensor echoes, either "assisting recovery" or arriving just late enough to claim salvage without contradiction. Station rumor paints them as necessary opportunists, tolerated because they know the blind spots between corporate liability and official response times. Whether they are simply quick to capitalize on abandoned tonnage or have a more intimate understanding of why certain ships go missing remains, for now, a matter of speculation.
zh: 在与弃船潮行者 TA-7207 同一批航道上活动的独立运货船员中，很少有名字像"第二航班"那样被频繁提起。这支船员以接别的船长会悄悄推掉的合同著称——把货物和打捞品运过那些巡逻覆盖变薄、导航数据不再与官方星图吻合的航线。他们没有注册为行会，也不设固定母港，可他们的应答器信号曾在贸易管理局资产附近不止一起"行政上未结"的事件中被记录在案。\n\n人们普遍认为"第二航班"这个名字是在指一次失败的首航，尽管标准登记册里显眼地找不到他们旗下任何更早飞船的记录。有据可查的是一个图案：每当那个星区有货船陷入沉寂，第二航班就从不远离下一批传感器回波——要么在"协助打捞"，要么来得刚好够晚，好无可争辩地认领打捞权。空间站的传言把他们说成是必要的机会主义者，被容忍是因为他们清楚企业责任与官方响应时间之间的盲区。他们究竟是单纯地迅速利用被遗弃的残骸，还是对某些飞船为何失踪有着更私密的了解，目前仍只是猜测。
